page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: only the right-hand ends of its lines are visible at the left edge, cut off by the gutter. Right page: one column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin beside lines 2 to 6, and a vertical row of quotation marks along the right edge of the text block. Running head at the top, page number at top right, catchword and gathering mark at the foot.

main_text.p: culentius constare possit. Sic ergo miserabi-lem ruentis Ecclesiæ statum deplorant illi:

Animaduertite inprimis, o Christicolæ, & ante Concil. Basil. Epist. synodal. ad vniuers. Christi fideles, de obediendo Concilijs ge-neralibus. oculos vestros ponite miserandum & flebilem sta-tum religionis Christianæ, si eo redacta fuerit, vt quisq; in summâ Pontificiâ positus, iam affecutus sit, quod nullam correctionem à Concilijs generali-bus habeat pertimescere, quantumcunq; Ecclesiam scandalizet, & eius statum perturbet, ac decolorét: ita vt si omnes dignitates Ecclesiasticas, & beneficia vendéret, si Prælatos quosq; inuitos transferret, & expelleret iniuste pro libito voluntatis, etiam notorie, ac iniuste Reges ac Principes deiiceret, moribus per-niciosis animas hominum passim perimere laboraret, crudelitates perpetraret horrendas, Legem Dei con-funderet, quaq; salubria instituta everteret, tempo-ralia Ecclesia Romana, & caeterarum particularium Ecclesiarum dissiparet, atq; alienaret; aliaq; immu-[?] mera flagitia, scelera, & crimina notoria perpetra-ret, ac se incorrigibilem redderet: Omnes Ecclesiae in vnam congregatâ, nullatenus eum à talibus coercere possit: quinimo liberum sit, quamlibet Synodum, eum reprimere volentem, illico transferre, vel dissoluere persistentes in Synodo contra volantem eius perse-qui, excommunicare, priuare, inhabilitare, contume-liâ & iniuriis afficere, inuasiones corporales ad-uersus eos excitare; deinde quicquid Synodus sta-tueret, præciperet, distaret, ordinaret, penitus con-temnere, abiicere, reprobare. Conspicite pro Dei re-uerentia, qualis ex hac re daretur iniuria in suam humani generis, ad subuertendam religionem Chri-stianam, dum seducendo vnum hominem, posset Chri-

page.notes: Left page: only the right-hand line ends are visible, cut off by the gutter. Each fragment is one visible line end, not a full line, so the left page's text cannot be read as running text. The blank line in the left fragments is a line with no visible ending. Right page: the central part of the text is covered by a dark smear and water damage, so the words in that area are uncertain. Doubtful readings: "vendéret" and "decolorét" (accents uncertain); "immu-" and "mera" at the line break, where the word may be "immane" or otherwise, and was not legible; "contra volantem" as printed, possibly "volentem". The quotation marks along the right edge of the text block are printed, but I could not read each one reliably and have not transcribed them. The "I" at the foot centre is taken as a gathering mark, which is uncertain. The catchword "Chri-" at the foot right ends the page at a hyphen.
